newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Standard Life's Irish unit's new premiums up 65pct.
newsitem.headline: Standard Life's Irish unit's new premiums up 65pct.

text.p: Standard Life's Irish operation reported new premiums of 41.5 million Irish pounds for the year to November 15, 1996 on Wednesday.
This represents a rise of 65 percent on the previous year, Standard Life said in a results statement.
It said the increase was made up of an 18 percent increase in regular premium income to 9.9 million Irish pounds and an 88 percent rise in single premium income to 31.6 million.
On the investment only pensions side, the Irish operation recorded a figure of more than 69 million Irish pounds compared to 12.5 million the previous year.
Annual premium income in personal pensions was up 0.2 million to 2.2 million while single premium income in this area increased to 4.8 million Irish pounds from 3.6 million in 1995.

"I am confident that we can keep this momentum going in the current financial year," general manager Alan Ashe said. "We have invested significantly in Ireland in terms of recruitment, training and IT over the past two years and this investment is beginning to pay off."
Standard Life said annual premium income rose by 22 percent to a record 5.4 million while single premiums in this area increased by 36 percent to 5.4 million.

It said its savings and life business in Ireland increased from a regular premium income to 1.6 million Irish pounds from 1.5 million. Single premium income in the bonds area rose to 13 million, a 97 percent increase on the 1995 outturn, it said.
" We continue to be one of the strongest players in Ireland in terms of both pensions and investment performance - a fact that is demonstrated by these excellent results across the board," Ashe said.
